samir: Heads-up - after landing the int4 conversion for the `mistralx-13b` variant I see a consistent quality dip on our long-context QA suite (winograd-like probes). Investigating now but flagging in case it's a conversion pattern.

louise: can you paste the minimal repro? numbers + diff would help.

samir: quick snippet below. baseline is fp16 `mistralx-13b` -> converted int4 via our converter v2.3. Observed that logits for token positions ~1020-1035 diverge sharply and answers flip.

samir: ```
# run eval harness
python eval/run_eval.py --model mistralx-13b-int4 --prompts tests/long_qa.jsonl \\n  --max-tokens 200 --batch 1 --kv-cache true --seed 42 > out_int4.log
python eval/run_eval.py --model mistralx-13b-fp16 --prompts tests/long_qa.jsonl \\n  --max-tokens 200 --batch 1 --kv-cache true --seed 42 > out_fp16.log
```

samir: diff shows huge KL at tokens 1024..1030. example: fp16 gives `Answer: 42`, int4 gives `Answer: 7` with high prob mass shift.

kai: interesting. did you try flipping kv-cache off to see if it's an attention/kv issue?

samir: yes - with `--kv-cache false` the gap disappears. it's a kv-cache dependent regression.

maya: could be kv-phase wrap or token-id offset creeping in conversion. any evidence of token-id remap?

samir: token ids match across tokenizer outputs. verified by `python -c 'print(list(tok.encode(s)[:1100])[-5:])'` for the troubling prompt. no shift.

louise: what about head-dim ordering / proj reorder in the converter? int4 codepath uses per-head packing kernel that assumes contiguous headpack. if ordering changed earlier we might be mixing heads at high position.

samir: converter logs show `layout=QKVH` -> `QKVH_packed` as expected. but i noticed a weird pattern: when we warm the kv cache (prefix caching) repeatedly the cached keys at index ~1024 appear to be a copy of earlier step (like a "snapback") causing mismatch.

kai: snapback? like the cache pointers wraparound at a power-of-two boundary? 1024 is suspicious.

samir: exactly the hypothesis. maybe an index masking bug in the pack kernel that uses `& (buffer_size-1)` somewhere.

maya: can you dump the raw kv tensors at steps 1018..1032 for both models and diff per-head? minimal binary dump + md5s is fine.

samir: doing that now. command: ```python -c "dump_kv('mistralx-13b-int4', prompt, out='kv_int4.npz', steps=[1018,1024,1030])"```

deploy-bot: scheduled nightly job `conv-smoke` for `mistralx-13b-int4` at 03:30 UTC.

samir: pasted head0 md5s: int4 step1024: a1f3... , step1030: b4c2... ; fp16 step1024: d9e8... , step1030: e7f1... so they diverge at the suspected window.

louise: can you also run with single-head view to see if only a subset of heads are affected? `--dump-heads 0,3,7,11`

samir: single-head dump shows heads 3 and 11 have identical md5 at step1024 and step100 earlier. looks like two heads got duplicated in cache.

maya: that smells like an in-place copy bug in the packing routine where stride calc uses int instead of int64 and overflows on large seq len. maybe only on packed int4 layout path.

kai: reproduction timeline: is this only with long prefix > 1k? test with zero-pad long repeating tokens to see when it triggers. if it's seqlen boundary dependent we can add guard in runtime.

samir: doing that now. quick test: seqlen 512 ok; seqlen 1024 reproduces; seqlen 1536 also reproduces. seems to trigger at >=1024 when buffer page crosses.

louise: action items: 1) create reduced reproducer that triggers just the packing code 2) run converter with debug symbols and ASAN build of runtime 3) schedule bisect on pack kernel change set range (last 3 months)

maya: i'll take (1). samir can you open a GH issue with the dumps + md5 + exact converter commit? put `eng-ml` label and set priority high.

samir: filed GH issue #4521 with attachments and trace. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4521

kai: pinging @sre-bot for an ephemeral debug build in the `int4-packing-debug` job.

sre-bot: received. created job `int4-packing-debug-#78` and attached logs to GH issue.

louise: one more theory: when KV cache uses blockwise memcpy we might be miscomputing destination offset for odd head counts. that could rationalize only certain heads duplicated. check head_count parity and aligned memcpy size.

samir: head_count=16 for this model. but our packing path reduces `head_pack = 8` when int4 packing applied. will probe parity mismatch.

maya: if confirmed, fix is likely small (offset calc) but we should add unit test that simulates wrap at buffer boundary and ensures unique MD5s per step.

samir: agreed. i'll run further bisect and update issue. thanks all :thumbsup:

louise: awesome. keep us posted. if you want I can start a rollback of converter v2.3 on dedicated cluster to pause exposure while fix lands.

samir: please do that after we confirm minimal repro. won't roll back until we have validated the hotfix.

kai: +1. schedule a short follow-up sync if needed.

maya: added a short checklist to the GH issue for QA steps.

samir: closing the loop here, i'll post final bisect commit once found.
